sections.normalized_html:
To calculate a percentage, we take the part as a fraction of the whole and then multiply the fraction by [MATH: 100\%.]

We will first calculate the percentage for undergraduates, then calculate the percentage for graduate students.

  • The total number of undergraduates is [MATH: 500 + 400 = 900,] and the number of undergraduates who preferred morning classes is [MATH: 280 + 210 = 490.] So, the percentage of undergraduates who preferred morning classes is [MATH: \dfrac{490}{900} \times 100\% \approx 54.4\%.]

  • Out of [MATH: 300] graduate students, the number who preferred morning classes is [MATH: 120.] So, the percentage of graduate students who preferred morning classes is [MATH: \dfrac{120}{300} \times 100\% = 40\%.]

Finally, the difference between the percentages is

[MATH: 54.4\% - 40\% = 14.4\%.]

Therefore, rounded to the nearest whole number, the difference is [MATH: 14\%.]
